columns.name: array_asset_name
columns.description: What `array_asset_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this array asset. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: conversion
columns.description: Multiply stored values by this before offset.

columns.name: coordinate_position_column
columns.description: Which column of that resource holds the 0-based position.

columns.name: coordinate_resource
columns.description: Resource whose rows are this axis's positions (labelled axis).

columns.name: coordinate_array_asset_id
columns.description: A 1-D array holding one value per position (irregular axis).

columns.name: coordinate_unit
columns.description: Unit of the numeric coordinate values.

columns.name: step_tick_den
columns.description: Denominator of the step, in ticks. Absent means 1.

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: Clock the ticks are counted on (regular tick axis).

columns.name: t_tick
columns.description: Spike tick on clock_id, mapped through core.clock_anchors.

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: The clock these ticks are on, normally the session's reference.

columns.name: time_bucket_tick
columns.description: First tick of the bucket this spike falls in, on clock_id.

rules.message: a spike precedes the start of the bucket it is labelled with
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id, t_tick, time_bucket_tick FROM analysis_spike_events WHERE time_bucket_tick > t_tick

rules.message: buckets overlap in tick range, so the layout they declare is not a partition
rules.sql: SELECT a.session_id, a.clock_id, a.time_bucket_tick AS earlier_bucket, a.hi, b.time_bucket_tick AS later_bucket, b.lo FROM (SELECT session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick, MIN(t_tick) AS lo, MAX(t_tick) AS hi FROM analysis_spike_events GROUP BY session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick) a JOIN (SELECT session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick, MIN(t_tick) AS lo, MAX(t_tick) AS hi FROM analysis_spike_events GROUP BY session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick) b ON a.session_id = b.session_id AND a.clock_id = b.clock_id AND b.time_bucket_tick > a.time_bucket_tick WHERE b.lo <= a.hi

columns.name: array_asset_name
columns.description: What `array_asset_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this array asset. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: conversion
columns.description: Multiply stored values by this before offset.

rules.message: scaling is declared both on the array and per channel
rules.sql: SELECT a.array_asset_id FROM core_array_assets a WHERE a.conversion IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_array_channels c WHERE c.array_asset_id = a.array_asset_id AND c.conversion IS NOT NULL)

rules.message: sample_rate_hz disagrees with the time axis step
rules.sql: SELECT a.array_asset_id, a.sample_rate_hz FROM core_array_assets a JOIN core_array_dimensions d USING (array_asset_id) JOIN core_clocks c ON c.clock_id = d.clock_id WHERE a.sample_rate_hz IS NOT NULL AND d.step_tick_num / COALESCE(d.step_tick_den, 1) IS NOT NULL AND c.tick_rate_hz IS NOT NULL AND abs(a.sample_rate_hz - c.tick_rate_hz / d.step_tick_num / COALESCE(d.step_tick_den, 1)) > 1e-6

columns.name: axis_index
columns.description: Axis that channel_index indexes, in stored order.

columns.name: inter_sample_shift
columns.description: Acquisition time offset within one sample period, in sample periods.

columns.name: unit
columns.description: Physical unit of the converted value.

columns.name: conversion
columns.description: Multiply stored values by this before offset.

rules.message: a conversion without a unit yields a number in no known quantity
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, channel_index FROM core_array_channels WHERE conversion IS NOT NULL AND unit IS NULL

columns.name: coordinate_position_column
columns.description: Which column of that resource holds the 0-based position.

columns.name: coordinate_resource
columns.description: Resource whose rows are this axis's positions (labelled axis).

columns.name: coordinate_array_asset_id
columns.description: A 1-D array holding one value per position (irregular axis).

columns.name: coordinate_unit
columns.description: Unit of the numeric coordinate values.

columns.name: step_tick_den
columns.description: Denominator of the step, in ticks. Absent means 1.

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: Clock the ticks are counted on (regular tick axis).

rules.message: axis_index is not contiguous from 0
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, COUNT(*) AS n_axes, MAX(axis_index) AS max_axis FROM core_array_dimensions GROUP BY array_asset_id HAVING MAX(axis_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(axis_index) <> 0

rules.message: an axis declares more than one coordinate form
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE (CASE WHEN origin_tick IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN origin_value IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN coordinate_array_asset_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN coordinate_resource IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 1

rules.message: a regular tick axis needs clock_id, origin_tick and step_tick_num
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE origin_tick IS NOT NULL AND (step_tick_num IS NULL OR clock_id IS NULL)

rules.message: a regular numeric axis needs origin_value, step_value and coordinate_unit
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE origin_value IS NOT NULL AND (step_value IS NULL OR coordinate_unit IS NULL)

rules.message: coordinate_resource and coordinate_position_column must be present together
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE (coordinate_resource IS NULL) <> (coordinate_position_column IS NULL)

rules.message: a core axis points outward at a non-core resource (R20 §5.1)
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, coordinate_resource FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE coordinate_resource IS NOT NULL AND coordinate_resource NOT LIKE 'core.%'

rules.message: a step denominator is not positive, so the step it defines is meaningless
rules.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, step_tick_den FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE step_tick_den IS NOT NULL AND step_tick_den <= 0

columns.name: anchor_index
columns.description: 0-based position in this clock's anchor sequence.

rules.message: anchors are declared for a clock with no parent
rules.sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.clock_id FROM core_clock_anchors a JOIN core_clocks c USING (clock_id) WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NULL

rules.message: anchor_index is not contiguous from 0
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(anchor_index) AS hi FROM core_clock_anchors GROUP BY clock_id HAVING MAX(anchor_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(anchor_index) <> 0

rules.message: anchor sequences do not increase together, so interpolation is undefined
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id, anchor_index FROM ( SELECT *, LAG(t_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY clock_id ORDER BY anchor_index) AS prev_t, LAG(parent_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY clock_id ORDER BY anchor_index) AS prev_p FROM core_clock_anchors) WHERE prev_t IS NOT NULL AND (t_tick <= prev_t OR parent_tick <= prev_p)

rules.message: an anchor gap exceeds twice the median, leaving ticks the mapping does not define (R27 5.3)
rules.sql: WITH gaps AS (SELECT clock_id, anchor_index, t_tick - LAG(t_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY clock_id ORDER BY anchor_index) AS gap FROM core_clock_anchors), typical AS (SELECT clock_id, median(gap) AS m FROM gaps WHERE gap IS NOT NULL GROUP BY clock_id) SELECT g.clock_id, g.anchor_index, g.gap, t.m FROM gaps g JOIN typical t USING (clock_id) WHERE g.gap IS NOT NULL AND g.gap > t.m * 2

rules.message: stop_tick precedes start_tick
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, clock_id, start_tick, start_tick, stop_tick FROM core_clock_observation_intervals WHERE stop_tick < start_tick

rules.message: observation windows overlap, which would double-count observed time
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, clock_id, start_tick, start_tick, stop_tick FROM (SELECT *, LAG(stop_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY session_id, clock_id ORDER BY start_tick) AS prev_stop FROM core_clock_observation_intervals) WHERE prev_stop IS NOT NULL AND start_tick <= prev_stop

columns.name: clock_name
columns.description: What `clock_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this clock. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: tick_rate_hz
columns.description: Tick rate as float, required unless exact tick rate provided.

columns.name: tick_zero_utc
columns.description: Wall-clock instant of tick 0 on this clock.

columns.name: transform_slope
columns.description: Parent ticks per this clock's tick, as measured.

columns.name: transform_offset
columns.description: Parent-clock tick at this clock's tick 0.

rules.message: neither tick_rate_hz nor an exact rational rate is present
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id FROM core_clocks WHERE tick_rate_hz IS NULL AND (tick_rate_num IS NULL OR tick_rate_den IS NULL)

rules.message: tick rate is not positive
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id, tick_rate_hz, tick_rate_num, tick_rate_den FROM core_clocks WHERE tick_rate_hz <= 0 OR tick_rate_num <= 0 OR tick_rate_den <= 0

rules.message: transform_slope and transform_offset must be present together
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id FROM core_clocks WHERE (transform_slope IS NULL) <> (transform_offset IS NULL)

rules.message: a clock transform is declared without a parent clock
rules.sql: SELECT clock_id FROM core_clocks WHERE parent_clock_id IS NULL AND transform_slope IS NOT NULL

rules.message: tick_zero_utc is more than a day from session_start_time
rules.sql: SELECT c.clock_id, c.tick_zero_utc, s.session_start_time FROM core_clocks c JOIN core_sessions s USING (session_id) WHERE c.tick_zero_utc IS NOT NULL AND s.session_start_time IS NOT NULL AND (c.tick_zero_utc < s.session_start_time - INTERVAL 1 DAY OR c.tick_zero_utc > s.session_start_time + INTERVAL 1 DAY)

rules.message: a clock declares both a linear transform and anchor points
rules.sql: SELECT c.clock_id FROM core_clocks c WHERE c.transform_slope IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_anchors a WHERE a.clock_id = c.clock_id)

rules.message: a clock is its own ancestor, so walking the chain does not terminate (R27 3)
rules.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(clock_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT clock_id, parent_clock_id, 1 FROM core_clocks WHERE parent_clock_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT u.clock_id, c.parent_clock_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up u JOIN core_clocks c ON c.clock_id = u.ancestor WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT DISTINCT clock_id FROM up WHERE ancestor = clock_id OR depth >= 64

rules.message: a non-reference clock declares no alignment, so it cannot be converted (R27 4)
rules.sql: SELECT c.clock_id FROM core_clocks c JOIN core_sessions s USING (session_id) WHERE s.reference_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND c.clock_id <> s.reference_clock_id AND c.transform_slope IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_anchors a WHERE a.clock_id = c.clock_id)

columns.name: curation_name
columns.description: What `curation_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this curation. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced this record, where provenance is recorded.

columns.name: device_name
columns.description: What `device_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this device. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: session_id
columns.description: Session if device record is session-scoped.

columns.name: coordinate_frame
columns.description: The frame these coordinates are in.

columns.name: x_um
columns.description: X in micrometres, in that frame.

columns.name: electrode_name
columns.description: What `electrode_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this electrode. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: local_electrode_label
columns.description: Opaque source label; undefined base, not an offset.

columns.name: local_channel_label
columns.description: Opaque source label; undefined base, not an offset.

columns.name: start_tick
columns.description: First observed tick, on the stream's clock.

columns.name: stop_tick
columns.description: Last observed tick, on the stream's clock.

rules.message: stop_tick precedes start_tick
rules.sql: SELECT event_stream_id, start_tick, start_tick, stop_tick FROM core_event_stream_observation_intervals WHERE stop_tick < start_tick

rules.message: observation windows overlap, which would double-count observed time
rules.sql: SELECT event_stream_id, start_tick, start_tick, stop_tick FROM (SELECT *, LAG(stop_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY event_stream_id ORDER BY start_tick) AS prev_stop FROM core_event_stream_observation_intervals) WHERE prev_stop IS NOT NULL AND start_tick <= prev_stop

columns.name: event_stream_name
columns.description: What `event_stream_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this event stream. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: device_id
columns.description: The device that produced it, where one is identified.

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: The clock its events are timed on.

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced it. Null means it came off the device as recorded. A narrow exception to R9 §4: the manifest records outputs per resource and cannot distinguish streams within one table.

rules.message: streams carry no observation intervals and their clock declares none, so no rate over them has a denominator
rules.sql: SELECT s.event_stream_id, s.name FROM core_event_streams s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_event_stream_observation_intervals o WHERE o.event_stream_id = s.event_stream_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_observation_intervals c WHERE c.session_id = s.session_id AND c.clock_id = s.clock_id)

columns.name: event_name
columns.description: What `event_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this event. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: stream_id
columns.description: The stream this event belongs to.

rules.message: an event's clock_id disagrees with its stream's
rules.sql: SELECT e.session_id, e.event_id, e.clock_id, s.clock_id AS stream_clock_id FROM core_events e JOIN core_event_streams s ON e.stream_id = s.event_stream_id WHERE e.clock_id <> s.clock_id

rules.message: events fall outside the observation window in force for their stream
rules.sql: WITH stream_windows AS ( SELECT o.event_stream_id, o.start_tick, o.stop_tick FROM core_event_stream_observation_intervals o UNION ALL SELECT s.event_stream_id, c.start_tick, c.stop_tick FROM core_event_streams s JOIN core_clock_observation_intervals c ON c.session_id = s.session_id AND c.clock_id = s.clock_id WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM core_event_stream_observation_intervals o WHERE o.event_stream_id = s.event_stream_id ) ), observed AS ( SELECT DISTINCT event_stream_id FROM stream_windows ) SELECT e.session_id, e.event_id, e.stream_id, e.t_tick FROM core_events e JOIN observed k ON e.stream_id = k.event_stream_id LEFT JOIN stream_windows w ON e.stream_id = w.event_stream_id AND e.t_tick BETWEEN w.start_tick AND w.stop_tick WHERE w.start_tick IS NULL

columns.name: media_asset_name
columns.description: What `media_asset_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this media asset. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: activity_type
columns.description: Which kind of output this preference is about. Open, as R9 §6 leaves it.

columns.name: scope_kind
columns.description: The resource whose primary key `scope` holds, as a dotted resource ID (R49 §2.2). Open.

columns.name: scope
columns.description: What it applies to -- a probe_id, an array_asset_id, a camera -- or the session_id itself where the preference is session-wide.

rules.message: a preference names a run whose activity_type differs from the preference's
rules.sql: SELECT p.session_id, p.activity_type, p.scope, r.activity_type FROM core_preferred_runs p JOIN core_processing_runs r USING (processing_run_id) WHERE r.activity_type IS DISTINCT FROM p.activity_type

rules.message: a preference names a run belonging to another session
rules.sql: SELECT p.session_id, p.processing_run_id, r.session_id FROM core_preferred_runs p JOIN core_processing_runs r USING (processing_run_id) WHERE r.session_id IS NOT NULL AND r.session_id IS DISTINCT FROM p.session_id

rules.message: the preferred run is superseded by another run
rules.sql: SELECT p.session_id, p.activity_type, p.scope, p.processing_run_id FROM core_preferred_runs p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_processing_runs r WHERE r.supersedes_run_id = p.processing_run_id)

rules.message: a scope names a resource of its declared kind that does not exist (R49 §2.5)
rules.sql: WITH known AS (SELECT 'core.sessions' AS kind, session_id AS id FROM core_sessions UNION ALL SELECT 'core.probes', probe_id FROM core_probes UNION ALL SELECT 'core.array_assets', array_asset_id FROM core_array_assets UNION ALL SELECT 'core.devices', device_id FROM core_devices UNION ALL SELECT 'core.event_streams', event_stream_id FROM core_event_streams UNION ALL SELECT 'core.electrodes', electrode_id FROM core_electrodes) SELECT session_id, activity_type, scope_kind, scope FROM core_preferred_runs r WHERE r.scope_kind IN (SELECT DISTINCT kind FROM known) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM known k WHERE k.kind = r.scope_kind AND k.id = r.scope)

columns.name: probe_name
columns.description: What `probe_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this probe. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: source_file_id
columns.description: A source file the run consumed.

columns.name: processing_run_name
columns.description: What `processing_run_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this processing run. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: activity_type
columns.description: import, validation, sorting, curation, materialization, etc.

columns.name: scope
columns.description: What this run is about -- a probe_id, an array_asset_id, a camera -- or the session_id itself where the run is session-wide. Open, as activity_type is.

columns.name: scope_kind
columns.description: The resource whose primary key `scope` holds, as a dotted resource ID -- `core.probes`, `core.array_assets`. Open (R8 §4); a value naming no declared resource means the scope is not a packet resource. Set with `scope` or not at all.

columns.name: supersedes_run_id
columns.description: The run this one replaces, if any.

rules.message: a failed run is recorded in a committed packet
rules.sql: SELECT processing_run_id, activity_type FROM core_processing_runs WHERE status = 'failed'

rules.message: a materialization run does not record the software that produced it
rules.sql: SELECT processing_run_id, software_name, software_version FROM core_processing_runs WHERE activity_type = 'materialization' AND (software_name IS NULL OR software_version IS NULL)

rules.message: a run supersedes_run_id itself
rules.sql: SELECT processing_run_id FROM core_processing_runs WHERE supersedes_run_id = processing_run_id

rules.message: the supersedes chain contains a cycle
rules.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(processing_run_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT processing_run_id, supersedes_run_id, 1 FROM core_processing_runs WHERE supersedes_run_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT u.processing_run_id, r.supersedes_run_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up u JOIN core_processing_runs r ON r.processing_run_id = u.ancestor WHERE r.supersedes_run_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT DISTINCT processing_run_id FROM up WHERE ancestor = processing_run_id OR depth >= 64

rules.message: several runs share an activity and scope and none is preferred, so a consumer cannot choose between them
rules.sql: WITH grouped AS ( SELECT session_id, activity_type, scope, count(*) AS n FROM core_processing_runs WHERE scope IS NOT NULL GROUP BY session_id, activity_type, scope HAVING count(*) > 1) SELECT g.session_id, g.activity_type, g.scope, g.n FROM grouped g WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM core_preferred_runs p WHERE p.activity_type = g.activity_type AND p.scope = g.scope AND (p.session_id = g.session_id OR (p.session_id IS NULL AND g.session_id IS NULL)))

rules.message: an activity has several runs and at least one records no scope, so whether they compete cannot be determined
rules.sql: WITH per_activity AS ( SELECT session_id, activity_type, count(*) AS n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE scope IS NULL) AS unscoped FROM core_processing_runs GROUP BY session_id, activity_type) SELECT session_id, activity_type, n, unscoped FROM per_activity WHERE n > 1 AND unscoped > 0

rules.message: a run declares one half of its scope; the pair is what carries the meaning (R49 §2.4)
rules.sql: SELECT processing_run_id, scope_kind, scope FROM core_processing_runs WHERE (scope IS NULL) <> (scope_kind IS NULL)

rules.message: a scope names a resource of its declared kind that does not exist (R49 §2.5)
rules.sql: WITH known AS (SELECT 'core.sessions' AS kind, session_id AS id FROM core_sessions UNION ALL SELECT 'core.probes', probe_id FROM core_probes UNION ALL SELECT 'core.array_assets', array_asset_id FROM core_array_assets UNION ALL SELECT 'core.devices', device_id FROM core_devices UNION ALL SELECT 'core.event_streams', event_stream_id FROM core_event_streams UNION ALL SELECT 'core.electrodes', electrode_id FROM core_electrodes) SELECT processing_run_id, scope_kind, scope FROM core_processing_runs r WHERE r.scope_kind IN (SELECT DISTINCT kind FROM known) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM known k WHERE k.kind = r.scope_kind AND k.id = r.scope)

columns.name: session_name
columns.description: What `session_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this session. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: session_start_time
columns.description: Session start time if known; if unknown use explicit null only in non-strict test packets.

columns.name: session_end_time
columns.description: When the session ended, UTC. Metadata, not derived from the tables (R25 5).

columns.name: reference_clock_id
columns.description: The clock this session's times are reported on by default (R27 2).

columns.name: t_zero_tick
columns.description: Earliest observed tick, on `reference_clock_id`; the origin seconds count from.

rules.message: the manifest's session inventory and core.sessions disagree; the manifest names a session by its session_name, since an assigned session_id means nothing outside the packet that assigned it (R53 §2.3.1)
rules.sql: SELECT session_name FROM core_sessions WHERE session_name NOT IN (SELECT session_id FROM manifest_sessions) UNION ALL SELECT session_id FROM manifest_sessions WHERE session_id NOT IN (SELECT session_name FROM core_sessions)

rules.message: session_end_time precedes session_start_time
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, session_start_time, session_end_time FROM core_sessions WHERE session_end_time < session_start_time

rules.message: a session declaring more than one clock names no reference clock (R27 2)
rules.sql: SELECT s.session_id, COUNT(*) AS n_clocks FROM core_sessions s JOIN core_clocks c USING (session_id) WHERE s.reference_clock_id IS NULL GROUP BY s.session_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

rules.message: a clock does not reach the session's reference clock, so it cannot be converted to it
rules.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(clock_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT clock_id, clock_id, 0 FROM core_clocks UNION ALL SELECT u.clock_id, c.parent_clock_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up u JOIN core_clocks c ON c.clock_id = u.ancestor WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT c.session_id, c.clock_id FROM core_clocks c JOIN core_sessions s USING (session_id) WHERE s.reference_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM up u WHERE u.clock_id = c.clock_id AND u.ancestor = s.reference_clock_id)

columns.name: sorting_run_name
columns.description: What `sorting_run_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this sorting run. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: clock_id
columns.description: Clock the run's spike ticks are counted on.

columns.name: processing_run_id
columns.description: The run that produced this record, where provenance is recorded.

columns.name: amplitude_unit
columns.description: Unit of core.spike_events.amplitude for this run, e.g. uV, adc.

rules.message: spikes carry amplitudes but the sorting run declares no amplitude_unit
rules.sql: SELECT DISTINCT s.sorting_run_id FROM core_spike_events s JOIN core_sorting_runs r USING (sorting_run_id) WHERE s.amplitude IS NOT NULL AND r.amplitude_unit IS NULL

columns.name: source_file_name
columns.description: What `source_file_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this source file. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

rules.message: negative ticks on a clock with no absolute reference
rules.sql: SELECT s.session_id, s.clock_id, MIN(s.t_tick) AS min_tick FROM core_spike_events s JOIN core_clocks c USING (clock_id) WHERE s.t_tick < 0 AND c.tick_zero_utc IS NULL GROUP BY s.session_id, s.clock_id

rules.message: spikes fall outside the observation window in force for their unit
rules.sql: WITH unit_windows AS ( SELECT o.session_id, o.unit_id, o.sorting_run_id, o.curation_id, o.start_tick, o.stop_tick FROM core_unit_observation_intervals o UNION ALL SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id, u.sorting_run_id, u.curation_id, c.start_tick, c.stop_tick FROM core_units u JOIN core_sorting_runs r ON u.session_id = r.session_id AND u.sorting_run_id = r.sorting_run_id JOIN core_clock_observation_intervals c ON c.session_id = r.session_id AND c.clock_id = r.clock_id WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM core_unit_observation_intervals o WHERE o.session_id = u.session_id AND o.unit_id = u.unit_id AND o.sorting_run_id = u.sorting_run_id AND o.curation_id = u.curation_id ) ), observed AS ( SELECT DISTINCT session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id FROM unit_windows ) SELECT s.session_id, s.unit_id, s.sorting_run_id, s.curation_id, s.t_tick FROM core_spike_events s JOIN observed k ON s.session_id = k.session_id AND s.unit_id = k.unit_id AND s.sorting_run_id = k.sorting_run_id AND s.curation_id = k.curation_id LEFT JOIN unit_windows w ON s.session_id = w.session_id AND s.unit_id = w.unit_id AND s.sorting_run_id = w.sorting_run_id AND s.curation_id = w.curation_id AND s.t_tick BETWEEN w.start_tick AND w.stop_tick WHERE w.start_tick IS NULL

columns.name: subject_name
columns.description: What `subject_id` stands for: the identifier a source or an earlier packet used for this subject. The only bridge between two packets that numbered it differently (R53 §2.5).

columns.name: start_tick
columns.description: First tick of the trial, inclusive, on `clock_id`.

columns.name: stop_tick
columns.description: Last tick of the trial, inclusive, on `clock_id`.

rules.message: stop_tick precedes start_tick
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, trial_id, start_tick, stop_tick FROM core_trials WHERE stop_tick < start_tick

columns.name: coordinate_frame
columns.description: The frame these coordinates are in. Open, as R19 §3 left it.

columns.name: x_um
columns.description: X in micrometres, in that frame.

columns.name: electrode_id
columns.description: An electrode this unit was detected on.

columns.name: channel_index
columns.description: 0-based position of this electrode in the unit's channel list, where a dense array axis is indexed by it (R20 §2). Nothing joins on it.

columns.name: is_primary
columns.description: Whether this is the unit's peak electrode.

rules.message: a unit designates more than one peak electrode (R28 2)
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM core_unit_electrodes WHERE is_primary GROUP BY session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

rules.message: channel_index is not contiguous from 0, so a dense axis indexed by it addresses rows that are not there
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(channel_index) AS hi FROM core_unit_electrodes WHERE channel_index IS NOT NULL GROUP BY session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id HAVING MAX(channel_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(channel_index) <> 0

rules.message: stop_tick precedes start_tick
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id, start_tick, start_tick, stop_tick FROM core_unit_observation_intervals WHERE stop_tick < start_tick

rules.message: observation windows overlap, which would double-count observed time
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id, start_tick, start_tick, stop_tick FROM (SELECT *, LAG(stop_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id ORDER BY start_tick) AS prev_stop FROM core_unit_observation_intervals) WHERE prev_stop IS NOT NULL AND start_tick <= prev_stop

columns.name: source
columns.description: What produced the label, e.g. kilosort, decoder, bombcell.

columns.name: normalized_label
columns.description: Declared projection onto the closed set. Null where the source's label does not project.

columns.name: confidence
columns.description: The source's confidence, where it reports one.

rules.message: a (source, label) pair projects onto more than one normalized_label
rules.sql: SELECT source, label, COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(normalized_label, '')) AS distinct_projections FROM core_unit_quality_labels GROUP BY source, label HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(normalized_label, '')) > 1

columns.name: local_unit_label
columns.description: Opaque source label; undefined base, not an offset.

columns.name: quality_label_source
columns.description: Which core.unit_quality_labels source the designated label came from.

columns.name: n_spikes
columns.description: Total spikes for this unit in this context.

rules.message: n_spikes, first_spike_tick or last_spike_tick disagrees with core.spike_events
rules.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id FROM core_units u LEFT JOIN ( SELECT session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(t_tick) AS lo, MAX(t_tick) AS hi FROM core_spike_events GROUP BY session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id ) s USING (session_id, unit_id, sorting_run_id, curation_id) WHERE (u.n_spikes IS NOT NULL AND u.n_spikes IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(s.n, 0)) OR (u.first_spike_tick IS NOT NULL AND u.first_spike_tick IS DISTINCT FROM s.lo) OR (u.last_spike_tick IS NOT NULL AND u.last_spike_tick IS DISTINCT FROM s.hi)

rules.message: the designated quality label is not among the recorded ones
rules.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id, u.quality_label, u.quality_label_source FROM core_units u LEFT JOIN core_unit_quality_labels q ON u.session_id = q.session_id AND u.unit_id = q.unit_id AND u.sorting_run_id = q.sorting_run_id AND u.curation_id = q.curation_id AND u.quality_label = q.normalized_label AND u.quality_label_source = q.source WHERE u.quality_label IS NOT NULL AND q.source IS NULL

rules.message: quality_label and quality_label_source must be present together
rules.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id FROM core_units WHERE (quality_label IS NULL) <> (quality_label_source IS NULL)

rules.message: units carry no observation intervals and their clock declares none, so no rate over them has a denominator
rules.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id, u.sorting_run_id, u.curation_id FROM core_units u JOIN core_sorting_runs r ON u.sorting_run_id = r.sorting_run_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_unit_observation_intervals o WHERE o.session_id = u.session_id AND o.unit_id = u.unit_id AND o.sorting_run_id = u.sorting_run_id AND o.curation_id = u.curation_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_observation_intervals c WHERE c.session_id = u.session_id AND c.clock_id = r.clock_id)

rules.message: the designated electrode is not one the unit was detected on (R28 2.1)
rules.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id, u.sorting_run_id, u.curation_id, u.default_electrode_id FROM core_units u WHERE u.default_electrode_id IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_unit_electrodes e WHERE e.session_id = u.session_id AND e.unit_id = u.unit_id AND e.sorting_run_id = u.sorting_run_id AND e.curation_id = u.curation_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_unit_electrodes e WHERE e.session_id = u.session_id AND e.unit_id = u.unit_id AND e.sorting_run_id = u.sorting_run_id AND e.curation_id = u.curation_id AND e.electrode_id = u.default_electrode_id)
